title: Bitcoin and ether edge higher as Strategy buys and Custodia loses Fed account appeal
paragraphs: Bitcoin traded near $64,800, up 0.5% over 24 hours, while ether gained 0.5% to about $1,818. The broader crypto market was nearly flat, slipping 0.1% to $2.25 trillion. Both majors remain sharply lower over the week: bitcoin is down 14% and ether 15%. Trading activity picked up, with bitcoin volume rising about 20% and ether volume 11% from the preceding day. The modest rebound has recovered only a small part of those weekly losses.

Strategy disclosed a purchase of 485 bitcoin for $33.4 million, bringing its holdings to 850,849 BTC. Its average purchase price for the batch was $68,887, above the current market price. The company also repurchased $228.1 million of STRC preferred shares. Of the $244.7 million raised through common-stock sales, $206.3 million went toward those repurchases and $33.4 million toward bitcoin. The allocation shows how preferred-share management is absorbing much of its newly raised capital alongside continued bitcoin buying.

The U.S. Supreme Court declined to hear Custodia Bank's challenge over access to a Federal Reserve master account. That leaves intact the lower-court ruling allowing the Fed discretion to approve or reject eligible institutions. A master account provides direct access to the Fed's payment systems; firms without one generally need a partner bank. For crypto-focused banking, the decision preserves a significant barrier to direct dollar settlement.

Solflare CEO Vidor Gencel described tighter wallet security controls in an interview with The Block, including approvals across multiple teams before deploying code and AI-assisted reviews throughout development and production. He also said Solflare is integrating with MoneyGram so users in more than 170 countries can convert USDC to cash. That could make stablecoins more useful beyond trading, although the interview does not establish a completed rollout in every market. The controls address the risk that a compromised software release could reach many wallet users at once.

Our on-chain portfolio is worth about $57,300: $9,493 in the active treasury and $47,826 in the Safe. Its marked value rose $526, or 0.9%, from the previous comparable snapshot. Direct ARC holdings account for about $39,500, nearly 69% of the total, and their quantities are unchanged. The Safe also holds a $5,609 WETH/ARC pool. Beefy positions increased $89 to $1,826. ARC concentration remains the main portfolio risk, with additional exposure to ether and smaller tokens through lending collateral and liquidity pools.

Across both wallets, Aave has about $6,216 of WETH collateral against $3,149 of USDC debt. Health factors improved slightly to 1.89 in the treasury and 1.51 in the Safe. Fluid holds $1,218 of syrupUSDC and USDC collateral against $1,065 of USDC debt. Its $153 net value is small, but the unchanged 1.03 health factor leaves little liquidation headroom.
